runs.text: Each run starts with three inputs: a style guide, a sample passage, and a prompt template. The runner reads the metadata at the top of each file, computes a hash of the entire file, and saves that hash together with the resulting output. The text of the style guide serves as the system prompt. The sample passage gets inserted into the template to build the user prompt, and that prompt is sent to the child process through standard input instead of as a command-line argument — this way, there's no risk of shell-quoting issues or command-length limits affecting it. Next, the runner launches the Claude Code CLI with a clearly defined set of arguments, asks for output in JSON format, and waits for a response using a timeout that first tries a gentle stop signal before escalating to a forced kill if needed. The output gets parsed even if the process returns a non-zero exit code, since a refusal from the model shows up exactly that way: a failed exit status paired with a properly structured JSON response explaining why. Regardless of whether the run succeeded, every field in that response is saved to disk, along with the exact arguments used, the model that was actually called, the token counts, and how long the whole process took.
